editorial:
You wake up in a wooden box with almost no air, a dying phone, and a lighter. That is the whole world of this thriller, and it pulls you in fast. Ryan Reynolds plays Paul Conroy, an American truck driver in Iraq who is buried alive after an attack. There are no big sets or side characters; it is just him, the dark, and the ticking clock. The movie feels tight and stressful, but it keeps you curious because every call and sound matters. You feel his panic, but you also want to know who put him there and whether anyone will save him.

The acting is the main reason to watch. Reynolds carries the movie with fear, anger, and tired hope, while the camera stays close enough to make every breath feel real. The pacing is strong, with new problems arriving before you can relax. On the downside, the location can feel repetitive, and some phone calls are frustrating because help seems slow. Still, if you like tense survival stories, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Paul learns rescuers found a different buried hostage, Mark White, who did not survive. His phone dies, his air runs low, and the sounds above him are not a rescue. The movie ends with Paul still trapped and no help arriving. The twist is that the people he trusted were too late and focused on the wrong person, leaving his fate sealed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tense survival thrillers and single-location stories.
